name: Mouse
author: leonavas
description: The wireless mouse in the bar: how much battery it has left, and a slider for its pointer sensitivity behind a right click.

barWidget.description: Battery level for the wireless mouse, with a popup that carries a pointer-sensitivity slider. Left or right click opens it, middle click toggles the percentage, the wheel nudges sensitivity.

schema.label: Glyph
schema.description: Any Nerd Font character. Drawn in the bar while a mouse battery is being reported.

schema.label: Glyph while no battery is reported
schema.description: Shown when the mouse is off, asleep, or wired — the panel and its slider stay reachable behind it.

schema.label: Show the percentage next to the glyph
schema.description: Middle click on the icon toggles this too. Hidden on a vertical bar, which has no room for it.

schema.label: Remove the icon from the bar while no mouse battery is reported
schema.description: Off by default: with the icon always there, the sensitivity slider is always one right click away. UPower drops the device when a wireless mouse sleeps, so this makes the icon come and go through the day.

schema.label: Dim the icon while no mouse battery is reported
Colour the icon while the battery is low
schema.description: Uses the theme's urgent colour, like the rest of the bar.

schema.label: Notify once when the battery gets low
schema.description: One toast per discharge: it re-arms after the mouse is charged back above the threshold.

schema.label: What the slider moves
schema.description: "This mouse" writes a Hyprland per-device rule, leaving the touchpad and any second pointer on whatever input.lua gave them. "All pointers" writes input:sensitivity instead, which moves the touchpad along with the mouse.

schema.label: Hyprland device to write to
schema.description: Left empty, the pointer is guessed by matching `hyprctl devices` against the model name of the battery UPower is reporting. Set it to a name from `hyprctl devices` (e.g. logitech-x2-superstrike-1) to pin it — worth doing with two mice, or if Hyprland's -1 suffix shifts as devices are plugged in.

schema.label: Sensitivity
schema.description: The value the slider last set, from -1 (slowest) to +1 (fastest); 0 is the device's own default speed. Absent means the mouse follows the global input:sensitivity — the panel's Reset button puts it back.
